speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel weakness in your upper limbs and whether your double vision affects both eyes or just one. Additionally, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of diplopia worsened by specific gaze directions, fatigable limb weakness that improves with rest, and absence of sensory or balance deficits is classic for this neuromuscular junction disorder. I will proceed with a diagnosis based on this clinical evidence without further testing.
